title: Shopware Frontends template manifest
description: The single source of truth for which templates exist and what each one needs. Consumers read this instead of keeping their own list.

manifestVersion.description: Version of this contract. Bumped when field semantics change, so out-of-repo consumers can detect a manifest they do not understand.

notes.description: Anything that applies to every template.

id.description: Directory name under templates/. This is the identity used everywhere.

displayName.description: Human-readable name, for docs navigation, pickers and devcontainer labels.

packageName.description: The name field in the template's package.json. It does not always match the id, so consumers that filter workspaces need both.

purpose.description: One sentence on what this template is for.

docsUrl.description: Documentation page for this template. Null when no page exists, which is a gap worth closing rather than a valid state. Must resolve to a file under apps/docs/src/.

issueUrl.description: Prefilled link for reporting a problem with this template. The title is prefixed with the template id so issues arrive already triaged.

supportLevel.description: supported: receives feature work. example: builds in CI, no feature work, no support promise. deprecated: do not start new projects on it.

scaffoldable.description: Whether consumers may offer this template as a starting point for a new project. False when copying it out of the monorepo breaks (see notes), or when new projects must not start on it.

scaffoldCommand.description: Copies the template out of the monorepo into ./my-project. After running it: install dependencies with any package manager, then run the dev script. Null exactly when scaffoldable is false.

deployable.description: Whether this template is deployed to a hosting environment.

devcontainer.description: Whether .devcontainer/<id>/devcontainer.json exists, so it can be opened in GitHub Codespaces.

env.description: Env vars that point the template at your own Shopware instance. Every template ships with working demo-backend defaults, so none are needed for a first run.

node.description: The engines.node range from the template's package.json. Check it before installing.

devPort.description: Port the dev server listens on.

buildCommand.description: Contents of the build script in the template's package.json. Run the script through a package manager (npm run build), not this string directly.

devCommand.description: Contents of the dev script in the template's package.json. Starts a dev server, not a production one. Run the script through a package manager (npm run dev), not this string directly.

typeGeneration.description: How to regenerate the Store API types against your own instance, so they include its extensions. Set the env vars, run loadSchemaCommand to fetch the instance schema into api-types/, then run the script. Skipping the fetch makes the script fall back to the published default types. Null when the template does not wire @shopware/api-gen.

env.description: Env vars the schema fetch needs. Each description says how to derive the value from the storefront configuration, so a consumer does not have to ask for values it already has.

loadSchemaCommand.description: Fetches the instance's OpenAPI schema into api-types/. Executable as-is after dependencies are installed.

script.description: The package.json script that regenerates the types from the fetched schema.

notes.description: Anything a consumer needs to know that the fields above do not express.
